subject: Invoice question: October aggregation window & overage
messages:
From: Leah Park <leah@orchard.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 07:18:00 -0700
Subject: Question about October aggregation window on invoice

Hi Mateo,

I hope you're well — I'm reviewing Orchard's October invoice and we see a ~22% overage on the 'completion' endpoint compared to our internal logs. The bulk of the delta appears to be concentrated in the 00:00–02:00 UTC timeframe on Oct 3.

Two quick questions: (1) can you confirm what aggregation window Redwood uses when batching usage for metering (fixed calendar day vs rolling 24h cutoffs)? (2) can you run a breakdown of token counts per request for the Oct 3 period and share the export?

I'm attaching the invoice PDF we received (invoice_20261001.pdf) for reference. If there's an obvious explanation (time-zone alignment, duplicate sessions, etc.) we'll reconcile on our side; otherwise we'd like to escalate a potential adjustment.

Thanks — Leah
Leah Park
Head of Platform Ops, Orchard AI
[attachment: invoice_20261001.pdf (PDF, 320 KB)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Leah Park <leah@orchard.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about October aggregation window on invoice

Hi Leah — thanks for flagging this and for the invoice. I'm looping in Marissa from billing and Ben from metering so we can get a technical breakdown and a clean CSV export for the timeframe you called out.

Short answer up front: Redwood's metering uses per-request token counts that are aggregated into calendar-day buckets in UTC for invoicing. However, there are two places where apparent double-counting can appear: (1) when clients use both streaming and non-streaming variants in the same session (we count tokens on both the initial request and the resumed stream if the client doesn't ack), and (2) when near-edge retries are recorded as separate requests before the request ID de-dup window triggers.

I'll let Marissa/Ben pull the logs and confirm whether either pattern shows up on Oct 3. We'll share an export and our suggested next steps within the day.

— Mateo
Director, Account Success
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Leah Park <leah@orchard.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about October aggregation window on invoice

Hi Leah — I've pulled the Oct 1–10 usage for ORC-2025-83 and attached a per-request export focused on Oct 3 window you mentioned. Key findings while Ben continues the deeper check:

- We confirm the invoice aggregation is by UTC calendar day (00:00–23:59 UTC).
- The spike you see at ~00:30–01:20 UTC on Oct 3 is driven by ~1,100 short streaming sessions that each have an initial pre-roll request plus the live stream token accounting. Many of these sessions came from the same client IP range and appear to be retries from a client-side websocket reconnect attempting a resumed stream.
- Our metering dedupe window is 10s for request-level idempotency; streaming reconnects separated by >10s will be counted as separate requests.

Attachments: usage_export_20261011.csv (per-request rows: timestamp, request_id, client_ip, endpoint, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, session_type) — sample rows included at top. Also linking a short dashboard snapshot for the period: https://app.redwood.com/customers/ORC-2025-83/usage?range=2026-10-01_2026-10-10

Next steps we suggest: (A) if these reconnects are client-side behavior you can address, we can mark the flagged rows as 'non-billable' for this invoice as a one-time courtesy and apply a pro-rated credit; (B) otherwise, we can propose a defensive small-cap rolling de-dup policy by client IP to reduce future noise (requires product approval).

If you'd like the CSV filtered down to the exact request IDs we can generate a redacted extract for your legal/procurement team as well.

— Marissa
Senior Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: usage_export_20261011.csv (CSV, 2.1 MB)]

From: Leah Park <leah@orchard.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 13:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about October aggregation window on invoice

Thanks Marissa — this is really helpful and explains the shape of the spike. The reconnect behavior was an unintended change in our client release on Oct 2; we've already pushed a rollback but the traffic was real on Oct 3.

Given this, we'd like to request the one-time courtesy credit to correct the invoice. Can you confirm the credit amount if you mark all the flagged rows as non-billable? Also, if possible, please provide the redacted extract (request IDs and timestamps only) so our audit team can reconcile internally.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Leah
Head of Platform Ops, Orchard AI

Subject: Re: Question about October aggregation window on invoice

Leah — thanks for confirming the root cause. Marissa will generate the redacted extract and calculate the credit. For transparency / next steps:

1) Marissa will create a credit request ticket in our billing system referencing invoice_20261001.pdf and the flagged request IDs. Expect the ticket link in a follow-up email within 2 business days.
2) We will apply a one-time pro-rated credit on your next billing cycle if the flagged rows are accepted as non-billable. The credit estimate will be included in the ticket.
3) Ben will open a short internal product note about adjusting the streaming reconnect dedupe rules; any policy change would be opt-in for enterprise accounts and communicated in release notes.

If you need an immediate provisional credit for procurement purposes, we can issue a short-term invoice hold while the ticket is processed — let me know and I'll authorize it.

Best,
— Mateo
